question: What is the number of valence electrons in a graphite atom?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Four**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **graphite atom has four valence electrons. **
 
• **Graphite is an allotrope of carbon**, which has an atomic number of 6.
 
• The** number of valence electrons in an element can be determined by looking at its position in the periodic table**.
 
• The **electrons in the outermost shell of an atom are called valence electrons**.
 
• **Carbon has four electrons in its outermost shell, or valence shell**. 
 
• Carbon atoms form **chemical bonds with other atoms or groups of atoms to achieve a stable electron configuration**.
 
• Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds with other atoms
